emergencyAccepted.subject: Your trusted contact accepted
emergencyAccepted.title: Invitation accepted
emergencyAccepted.body: {{granteeEmail}} accepted to be your trusted contact for the emergency recovery of your encrypted data.
emergencyAccepted.note: There is nothing you need to do. You can revoke this role at any time from your encryption settings.

emergencyDeclined.subject: Your invitation was declined
emergencyDeclined.title: Invitation declined
emergencyDeclined.body: {{granteeEmail}} declined your invitation to become your trusted contact.
emergencyDeclined.note: You can designate someone else at any time from your encryption settings.

emergencyDesignated.subject: You have been designated as a trusted contact
emergencyDesignated.title: Trusted contact
emergencyDesignated.intro: {{grantorEmail}} designated you as their trusted contact for the emergency recovery of their encrypted data.
emergencyDesignated.role: The role is simple: if they permanently lose access to their data (devices and recovery phrase), they can request an emergency recovery. After a waiting period of {{waitTimeDays}} days, you would receive a recovery phrase to hand to them in person.
emergencyDesignated.privacy: This role never gives you access to any of their documents.
emergencyDesignated.decline: You are free to accept or decline this invitation.

emergencyRecoveryApprovedContact.subject: Emergency access granted
emergencyRecoveryApprovedContact.title: Access granted
emergencyRecoveryApprovedContact.body: The waiting period is over: your emergency access request regarding {{grantorEmail}} was approved.
emergencyRecoveryApprovedContact.todo: Retrieve the recovery phrase from the app, print it, then hand it to its owner in person.
emergencyRecoveryApprovedContact.privacy: On its own, this phrase gives you no access to their documents.

emergencyRecoveryApprovedGrantor.subject: Emergency access granted to your contact
emergencyRecoveryApprovedGrantor.title: Emergency access granted
emergencyRecoveryApprovedGrantor.body: The waiting period elapsed without a refusal: emergency access was granted to {{granteeEmail}}.
emergencyRecoveryApprovedGrantor.meaning: Concretely, they can now retrieve the recovery phrase meant to be handed to you in person. This phrase does not give them access to your documents.
emergencyRecoveryApprovedGrantor.revoke: You can still revoke this role from your encryption settings.

emergencyRecoveryCancelled.subject: Emergency access request cancelled
emergencyRecoveryCancelled.title: Request cancelled
emergencyRecoveryCancelled.body: {{granteeEmail}} cancelled their own emergency access request for your encrypted data.
emergencyRecoveryCancelled.note: No action is needed on your side.

emergencyRecoveryRejected.subject: Your emergency access request was refused
emergencyRecoveryRejected.title: Request refused
emergencyRecoveryRejected.note: Your trusted contact role remains in place. If a recovery becomes genuinely necessary, you can submit a new request.

emergencyRecoveryReminder.subject: Reminder: emergency access request in progress
emergencyRecoveryReminder.title: Reminder: emergency access
emergencyRecoveryReminder.intro_one: {{count}} day left before the automatic approval of the emergency access request from {{granteeEmail}}.
emergencyRecoveryReminder.intro_other: {{count}} days left before the automatic approval of the emergency access request from {{granteeEmail}}.
emergencyRecoveryReminder.expected: If this request is expected, there is nothing to do: just let the waiting period complete.
emergencyRecoveryReminder.unexpected: If this request is NOT expected, refuse it now. A simple login to your account is enough, no recovery phrase is needed.

emergencyRecoveryRequested.subject: Emergency access request for your data
emergencyRecoveryRequested.title: Emergency access request
emergencyRecoveryRequested.intro: {{granteeEmail}}, your trusted contact, requested emergency access to your encrypted data.
emergencyRecoveryRequested.deadline: Unless you refuse before {{deadline, long}}, access will be granted automatically at the end of the {{waitTimeDays}}-day waiting period.
emergencyRecoveryRequested.expected: If this request is expected, for instance because you lost your access, there is nothing to do: just let the waiting period complete.
emergencyRecoveryRequested.unexpected: If this request is NOT expected, refuse it now. A simple login to your account is enough, no recovery phrase is needed.

emergencyRevoked.subject: Your trusted contact role has ended
emergencyRevoked.title: Role ended
emergencyRevoked.body: {{grantorEmail}} ended your trusted contact role, or the relationship was removed.
emergencyRevoked.note: Any associated escrow was destroyed. No action is required on your side.

emergencyVaultRecovered.subject: Your access was restored through the emergency procedure
emergencyVaultRecovered.title: Recovery complete
emergencyVaultRecovered.body: Your vault was unlocked with the emergency phrase and a new personal phrase was set.
emergencyVaultRecovered.voided: The phrase held by {{granteeEmail}} is now void, and a fresh escrow automatically protects you again.
emergencyVaultRecovered.warning: If you did not perform this operation, contact your administrator. Note that it cannot happen without a login to your account.

emergencyVaultRecoveredContact.subject: Recovery complete, the phrase is now void
emergencyVaultRecoveredContact.title: Recovery complete
emergencyVaultRecoveredContact.body: The recovery you helped with for {{grantorEmail}} is complete.
emergencyVaultRecoveredContact.voided: The phrase you received is now void: you can discard it.
emergencyVaultRecoveredContact.note: A fresh escrow was created automatically. There is nothing you need to do.

vaultPurgeWarning.subject: Your previous encrypted vault will be deleted
vaultPurgeWarning.title: A previous vault will be deleted
vaultPurgeWarning.intro: On {{disabledAt, long}}, your encryption vault was replaced by a new one, or you stopped using encryption. That earlier vault can still be restored with its own recovery phrase.
vaultPurgeWarning.deadline: It will be permanently deleted on {{purgeAt, long}}, together with the keys it holds. Content encrypted only with those keys will no longer be readable.
vaultPurgeWarning.keep: To keep it, restore it with its recovery phrase before that date. It then becomes your current vault again.
vaultPurgeWarning.nothing: If you no longer need it, there is nothing to do.

vaultPurged.subject: Your previous encrypted vault was deleted
vaultPurged.title: A previous vault was deleted
vaultPurged.intro: The encryption vault you stopped using on {{disabledAt, long}} was deleted, as announced, together with the keys it held.
vaultPurged.consequence: Content encrypted only with those keys can no longer be decrypted. Your current vault, if you have one, is not affected.

browser_warning.message: Your browser ({{browser}} {{version}}) is out of date. To ensure the security of your encrypted data, please update your browser to version {{minVersion}} or higher.

onboarding.reset_success: Your previous keys have been disabled (not deleted). You can now set up new ones.
onboarding.explanation: To enable encryption on your account, you will need to save a recovery phrase in the next step. Without it, you could permanently lose access to your encrypted documents.
onboarding.existing_recovery_hint: You already enabled encryption on another device. Choose how to restore your keys on this device.
onboarding.btn_start_new_identity: Start over with a new identity
onboarding.title_previous_identity: A previous encryption identity was found
onboarding.step_up_phrase_kept: The recovery phrase you just saved stays valid: the setup finishes as soon as you have confirmed.
onboarding.previous_identity_detected: Your account had an encryption identity that is now disabled, probably turned off from another device or replaced. Its encrypted documents can still be recovered with its recovery phrase.
onboarding.previous_identity_hint: Restore it with that phrase, or start over with a new identity: the old documents then stay locked until you restore.
onboarding.previous_identity_contacts_title: Lost the phrase? Your trusted contacts can help
onboarding.previous_identity_contacts_text: Ask one of them to start an emergency recovery: once the waiting period is over, they can hand the phrase back to you.
onboarding.invalid_word_hint: It looks like one or more words are not in the recovery word list. Check the ones highlighted in red for typos.
onboarding.last_resort_warning: You will lose access to documents encrypted with your current keys. New keys will be generated so others can share encrypted documents with you again.
onboarding.last_resort_consequence_1: Documents encrypted with the old key will remain inaccessible until you recover its old recovery phrase (they are not deleted).
onboarding.last_resort_consequence_2: Other members of those documents will need to remove you and re-share access after your new keys are created.
onboarding.last_resort_consequence_3: A new key pair will be generated and you will need to back it up.
onboarding.confirm_fingerprint_to_delete: To confirm, type your current safety fingerprint:
onboarding.reactivate_confirm: This recovery phrase belongs to a previous vault (created {{date}}). Reactivating it will disable your current vault, which stays recoverable with its own phrase. Continue?
onboarding.reactivate_cancelled: Reactivation cancelled. Your current vault stays active.
onboarding.extensions_warning: Before continuing, check that the browser extensions you have installed are trustworthy. Extensions have broad access to page content and could potentially access your sensitive data. If in doubt, temporarily disable them.
onboarding.print_warning: CONFIDENTIAL. Keep this document in a safe place. Anyone with this phrase could eventually access your encrypted documents.
onboarding.last_resort_alert: If you are the only person with full access to an encrypted document, it may be lost for good.
onboarding.restore_description: Enter or paste your 24-word recovery phrase, keeping the words in their original order.
onboarding.backup_description: Save this phrase somewhere safe, such as a password manager. You can use it to restore access when you can't use another device. It won't be shown again.
onboarding.cancel_setup_text: Encryption setup isn't complete. If you leave now, encryption won't be enabled.
onboarding.de_enrolled_notice_one: This browser had not used encryption for more than {{count}} day, so it forgot your keys for safety. Connect it again with another of your devices or your recovery phrase.
onboarding.de_enrolled_notice_other: This browser had not used encryption for more than {{count}} days, so it forgot your keys for safety. Connect it again with another of your devices or your recovery phrase.
onboarding.enabled_description: You can now use encryption in LaSuite apps. You can manage your encryption settings anytime from your account.
onboarding.restored_description: This device can now use encryption.
onboarding.option_device_description: Approve access from a device where encryption is already set up.
onboarding.option_phrase_description: Use your previously saved recovery phrase.

demo.title: Fake Product (Encryption Demo)
demo.subtitle: Demonstrates VaultClient integration. Products use encrypt()/decrypt() via the SDK. Key management goes through encryption.
demo.section_onboarding_note: In production, opens encryption in a visible iframe.
demo.footer: This demo shows two integration layers: product operations via VaultClient (encrypt/decrypt/hasKeys), and privileged operations via encryption (generate/export/import/delete).

settings.title: Encryption
settings.no_keys: Set up encryption on this device first.
settings.remote_disabled_warning: This device still has your encryption keys. Turn encryption back on so others can share encrypted documents with you again.
settings.remote_diverged_warning: The encryption identity registered on the server for your account is different from this device's. Another device signed in as you may have changed or replaced it. Until this is resolved, this device and the server disagree about your identity.
settings.remote_never_warning: This device has local encryption keys that were never registered on the server. This usually means an earlier setup did not finish. These keys cannot be re-enabled, because there is no vault behind them: the only safe option is to remove them and set up encryption again from scratch.
settings.remote_never_hint: Removing these keys clears this device's unfinished setup so you can start over cleanly. If you have a recovery kit from a completed setup, you can restore from it afterwards.
settings.reconcile_onboard_fresh: Remove these keys and set up encryption again
settings.reconcile_diverged_hint: Keeping this device's identity re-registers it as the active one and disables the identity the other device set, which will then need to reconcile in turn. Using the server's identity discards this device's local keys and re-acquires the active one from another device or your recovery phrase.
settings.reconcile_adopt_confirm: This device's encryption keys will be deleted, and the identity registered on the server will be set up here instead, from another device or your recovery phrase.
settings.sync_integrity_failed: The encrypted data stored on the server for your account could not be verified, so this device has paused syncing it. You can keep working: this device uses its last verified copy. Changes such as trusting or not trusting a contact's encryption identity cannot be saved until this is resolved. If this message persists, contact support.
settings.emergency_phrase_live_one: {{emails}} obtained an emergency recovery phrase for your data, and it still opens it. Changing your recovery phrase below is what cancels it. They stay one of your trusted contacts.
settings.emergency_phrase_live_other: These trusted contacts obtained an emergency recovery phrase for your data, and it still opens it: {{emails}}. Changing your recovery phrase below is what cancels them. They stay your trusted contacts.
settings.change_phrase_emergency_note_one: This will also cancel the emergency phrase {{emails}} obtained. They stay your trusted contact and a new dormant emergency phrase is set up for them, which nobody can use until a new request goes through the waiting period.
settings.change_phrase_emergency_note_other: This will also cancel the emergency phrases obtained by {{emails}}. They stay your trusted contacts and new dormant emergency phrases are set up for them, which nobody can use until a new request goes through the waiting period.
settings.change_phrase_success: Store the new phrase somewhere safe. Your previous phrase stops working once you confirm below.
settings.change_phrase_warning: Changing your recovery phrase creates a new one. All existing backups of your current phrase (password manager, file, printout) will stop working. You will need to save the new one before it takes effect.
settings.change_phrase_confirm_saved: I have saved my new recovery phrase
settings.change_phrase_committed: Your recovery phrase has been changed. Your previous phrase and its backups no longer work.
settings.delete_warning_backup: Before continuing, make sure you have your recovery phrase or access on another device.
settings.disable_server_warning: Your documents will stay encrypted. Without a recovery method, you may permanently lose access to them.
settings.remote_disabled_title: Encryption is off for your account
settings.delete_scope_device_hint: You won't be able to open encrypted documents on this device anymore. You can restore access with your recovery phrase or another device.
settings.delete_scope_account_hint: You won't be able to encrypt or open encrypted documents. Others won't be able to share new encrypted documents with you.
settings.cancel_change_text: You have not saved the new recovery phrase yet. If you close now, your current phrase stays valid and nothing changes.

emergency.title: Trusted contacts
emergency.intro: Trusted contacts can help you recover access if you lose your recovery phrase and can no longer use any of your devices.
emergency.trusted_subtitle: People who can help you recover access to your encrypted documents.
emergency.trusted_empty: You have not designated any trusted contact yet.
emergency.granted_subtitle: People who have chosen you as a trusted contact.
emergency.granted_empty: Nobody has designated you as a trusted contact yet.
emergency.vault_inactive_note: This escrow is attached to a previous vault, not your current one.
emergency.trusted_requested_warning: {{email}} requested a recovery code to help you regain access. If you take no action, they'll receive it {{time}}.
emergency.trusted_approved_warning: {{email}} can now obtain your recovery code. You can still reject the request to lock it again.
emergency.audit_tampered: This emergency escrow does not match what you signed: it may have been tampered with on the server. Do not rely on this entry and contact support.
emergency.audit_stale: This contact's encryption identity has changed since the designation. The current escrow can no longer be used: renew it after verifying the contact's new identity.

emergency.granted_requested_text: You have requested emergency access. Unless the owner refuses, it will be granted {{time}}.
emergency.granted_approved_text: Access is granted. You can reveal {{email}}'s recovery phrase to hand it over to them.
emergency.reject_done: The request from {{email}} has been refused. Your vault stays locked for this contact.
emergency.confirm_revoke_body: The emergency escrow will be destroyed and {{email}} will no longer be able to help you recover access. This contact will be notified. You can designate them again later.
emergency.confirm_decline_body: The emergency escrow created by {{email}} will be destroyed and they will be notified. You will not be able to help them recover access.
emergency.confirm_request_body: {{email}} will be notified immediately and can refuse for {{count}} days. Only make this request to help them regain access to their documents: they are informed at every step.
emergency.prompt_recovery_title: Someone requested access to your encrypted data
emergency.prompt_recovery_body: {{email}}, one of your trusted contacts, requested emergency access to your encrypted data.
emergency.prompt_recovery_deadline: If you do nothing, access is granted on
emergency.prompt_recovery_approved: {{email}}, one of your trusted contacts, requested emergency access to your encrypted data, and the waiting period has elapsed, so it is now available to them.
emergency.prompt_recovery_hint: This recovery is meant to get you back in on a device that lost access. You are signed in here and your encryption already works, so it gains you nothing on this device.
emergency.prompt_recovery_hint_refuse: If you did not arrange it with this contact, refuse the request to re-lock your data.
emergency.prompt_invite_title: You have been designated as a trusted contact
emergency.prompt_invite_body: Someone trusts you to help them regain access to their encrypted documents if they lose their recovery phrase. Review the invitation below to accept or decline it.
emergency.prompt_signed_out_recovery: One of your trusted contacts requested emergency access to your encrypted data. Sign in to see who asked and when access would be granted, and to refuse the request if you did not arrange it.
emergency.prompt_signed_out_invite: Someone trusts you to help them regain access to their encrypted documents if they lose their recovery phrase. Sign in to review the invitation.
emergency.designate_intro: Search for the person by their exact email address. They must already use encryption.
emergency.designate_not_found: No account matches this address. Check the spelling, or ask the person to create their account first.
emergency.designate_not_onboarded: This person must set up encryption first (from a LaSuite product) before they can be designated as a trusted contact.
emergency.designate_verify_required: Before designating this contact, verify their identity: compare the fingerprint below through a trusted channel. This verification prevents a compromised server from substituting the contact's keys.
emergency.designate_untrusted: This contact is not verified yet. Compare their safety fingerprint through a trusted channel and approve it before designating them.
emergency.designate_wait_explanation: If this contact ever requests emergency access, you will be notified and can refuse during this period. If you do not respond, access will be granted when it ends.
emergency.designate_wait_hint: A period that is too short is risky: during long holidays you might not see the notification in time to refuse an illegitimate request.
emergency.designate_scope_title: What this contact will be able to do:
emergency.designate_scope_1: After the wait period, they will receive an emergency phrase to hand back to you in person, so that you unlock your own vault yourself.
emergency.designate_scope_2: They never see your documents and gain no access to your account.
emergency.designate_scope_3: You can revoke this designation at any time.
emergency.designate_success: The invitation has been sent to {{email}}. The designation takes effect once this contact accepts it.
emergency.reveal_instruction_1: Hand this phrase to its owner in person, or through an equally safe channel.
emergency.reveal_instruction_2: It gives you no access to their documents: only its owner can use it, once logged into their own account.
emergency.reveal_instruction_3: As soon as they use it, they will be required to replace it immediately: this phrase is single-use by design.
emergency.reveal_instruction_4: If the owner can no longer act themselves (for example an accident), it is only useful to whoever can also sign into their account: pass it on strictly through your organisation's established recovery process, to the team that manages logins, never to someone who simply asks.
emergency.reveal_untrusted_grantor: Before showing the phrase, make sure you are really helping {{email}}: compare the safety code below with them through a channel you trust (in person, or a call you started), then confirm it matches. This is what protects you from handing a phrase to the wrong person or one a compromised server tampered with.
emergency.btn_grantor_verified: The code matches, show the phrase
emergency.reveal_still_available: You can come back to this screen and show the phrase again for as long as the recovery stays granted, so nothing is lost if you close it.
emergency.rotation_explanation: You unlocked your vault with an emergency phrase handed over by your trusted contact. Because that contact has seen it, it must be replaced now: save the new phrase below, it will become the only valid one.
emergency.rotation_rearm_note: Your trusted contacts stay in place: a fresh emergency escrow is created automatically for each of them.
emergency.rotation_done: Your recovery phrase has been replaced. The emergency phrase that was used no longer works.
emergency.rearm_blocked: These contacts are no longer verified: {{emails}}. Their emergency escrow cannot be renewed until their identity is approved. You can revoke them to proceed, then designate them again later.
emergency.onboarding_done_text: Your keys are created and your recovery kit is saved.
emergency.nudge_text: You can also choose a trusted contact who can help you recover access if you lose your recovery phrase.

maintenanceTool.title: LaSuite Encryption: maintenance tool
maintenanceTool.intro: Turns the encrypted export a product team hands over into a decrypted copy, which the team imports back, with a maintenance phrase; also generates that phrase. Everything happens in this page: it cannot connect to any network, and nothing leaves this computer except the files you download. The maintenance escrow is a temporary mode for a massive loss (a technical failure, an organization stopping encryption); a user who lost their keys has their own recovery means, which let no one else read.
maintenanceTool.publicKeyHandoff: Give it to the team that runs the encryption service: they add it to MAINTENANCE_ESCROW_KEYS with the email domains it covers ("*" for every user), then check that the server's startup log shows the fingerprint below. It is not secret: send it by any means.

decrypt.folderHelp: The folder the product team handed over (written by its export command, maintenance_export in Docs and Drive), with manifest.ndjson at its root. It holds no plaintext.
decrypt.folderSeveralExports: This folder holds several encrypted exports side by side ({{folders}}): pick one of them.
decrypt.folderMissingFiles: {{count}} files named by the manifest are not in the folder, such as {{examples}}. Copy them from the object storage before decrypting, or those items will fail.
decrypt.phraseHelp: The 24 words generated when the maintenance escrow was set up for this deployment (or for your organization), kept by its custodians, on paper, a drive or a printed sheet. Type one word per box, or paste the whole phrase into the first box. The fingerprint shown below must match the one the server logs at startup for your organization.
decrypt.fingerprint: To compare with the digits the server logs at startup for your organization: the same, or the server escrows for another key.
decrypt.coverageAll: All {{roots}} documents of this encrypted export are escrowed for this phrase's key.
decrypt.coverageSome: {{ours}} of the {{roots}} documents of this encrypted export are escrowed for this phrase's key; the others will be set aside for their own custodians.
decrypt.coverageNone: None of the {{roots}} documents of this encrypted export is escrowed for this phrase's key. Check that this is your organization's phrase (its fingerprint must be the one the server logs for your organization), and that the encrypted export was made for your key (with the fingerprint above).
decrypt.runHelpFolder: The same folder, decrypted, to give back to the product team for import. Into a folder: each file is written as soon as it is decrypted, whatever the encrypted export weighs; pick where, and a new folder is created there. Into a .zip archive: one file to carry, built in this browser's storage when it has some, in memory otherwise.
decrypt.runHelpZip: The same folder, decrypted, to give back to the product team for import. This browser cannot write into a folder (Chrome and Edge can), so the decrypted copy is a .zip archive, built in this browser's storage and then saved where you choose: each file is written as soon as it is decrypted.
decrypt.noneForThisKey: Nothing was decrypted: all {{count}} items are escrowed for other keys. This phrase is probably not the one this encrypted export was made for.
decrypt.otherKeys: {{count}} items are escrowed for other maintenance keys (other organizations). The decrypted copy holds them still encrypted, one encrypted export per key (other-keys/<fingerprint>/), to hand to those keys' custodians:
decrypt.outputExists: {{folder}} already exists: choose another place, or move that folder away first.
decrypt.discardArchive: Delete the archive from this browser
decrypt.archiveInBrowser: The archive stays in this browser's storage until you delete it, or until this page is opened again: delete it once saved.
decrypt.plaintextWarning: The decrypted copy holds the content in plaintext. Keep it on this computer or the removable drive it goes back on, and delete it once the product team has imported it (maintenance_import in Docs and Drive).
decrypt.previewTooLarge: {{id}} is too large to preview here ({{size}}): open it from the decrypted copy.

generate.help: Run this once per maintenance key, on an isolated computer, when the deployment enables the maintenance escrow: usually one key for every user, or one per organization on a shared deployment. The phrase is the secret key: never keep it on a connected computer. Hand the public key to the team that runs the deployment: they add it to the server's MAINTENANCE_ESCROW_KEYS, with the email domains it covers ("*" for every user).
generate.phraseCopiesHelp: Keep it the way that suits the place: shown here to write by hand, copied, downloaded to a removable drive, or printed. Every copy is the secret key: a file or a sheet is kept like the paper, in the vault, and a printer that keeps its jobs is no place for it.
generate.copyFailed: This browser refused the copy: download the phrase or write it down.
generate.fingerprint: Once the server runs with this key, its startup log shows the same digits beside the organization's domains. They are also what you give the product team when you ask for an encrypted export: their export command keeps only the documents escrowed for this key (in Docs and Drive: maintenance_export --fingerprint followed by these digits).
generate.confirmTitle: Does a maintenance key already exist?
generate.confirmText: A new phrase replaces nothing on the server. If this deployment (or your organization) already has a maintenance key, documents keep being escrowed for it until the team that runs the service swaps in the new public key, and its phrase is still the one that opens them. Generate a key when there is none yet, or to replace the current one on purpose.
generate.confirmReplaceShown: The phrase shown below will be replaced by the new one: keep it first if it is in use.

publicKey.help: For custodians who hold a phrase but no longer have its public key, to hand it again to the team that runs the deployment. The public key is not secret; the phrase is.
publicKey.title: The public key of this phrase

phrase.label: Maintenance phrase
phrase.unknownWords: Not a word of the French or English list: word {{numbers}}. Check the spelling against the sheet.
phrase.invalid: Every word exists, but the phrase does not check out: a word is wrong or not in its place.

rotate.help: When your organization replaces its maintenance key (new custodians, a phrase to retire), every copy made for the current key is wrapped again for the new one; only then can the current phrase be destroyed. First generate the new key and have the team that runs the encryption service put its public key in place of the current one. The product team then exports the copies alone, with the current key's fingerprint (maintenance_export --keys-only --fingerprint <its 40 digits>), and writes back what this tab produces (maintenance_rotate).
rotate.folderTitle: 1. The encrypted export of the copies
rotate.folderHelp: The folder the product team handed over, with manifest.ndjson at its root: one line per document (or Drive tree) with its copy.
rotate.oldPhraseTitle: 2. The current phrase, the one being replaced
rotate.oldPhraseHelp: The 24 words that open the copies of this export. They stay needed until the product team confirms that no copy for this key is left.
rotate.newKeyHelp: The public key of the new phrase, as generated in the "Generate a maintenance key" tab (or found again in "Find a phrase's public key"). Paste it here.
rotate.newKeyInvalid: This is not a maintenance public key: {{error}}
rotate.newKeyFingerprint: To compare with the fingerprint the custodians of the new phrase noted, and with the one the server now logs for your organization.
rotate.sameKey: This is the public key of the current phrase: paste the new key's public key.
rotate.coverageSome: {{ours}} of the {{roots}} copies of this encrypted export are for the current key; the others are for other keys and will not be rotated (the encrypted export should be made for this key only, with its fingerprint).
rotate.otherKeys: {{count}} copies are for other maintenance keys and were not rotated.
rotate.noSecret: This file holds no secret, only copies wrapped for a maintenance key: it can go back to the product team on any drive. Keep the current phrase until the product team confirms that no copy for its key is left (an export with its fingerprint comes back empty), then destroy it.
